raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like to change too much. What worked on my land before is still what I trust most. On these 8 mu, I will still keep the land split the usual way: most of it in wheat followed by summer maize, and a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize keep grain coming, and cotton gives some cash if the price is not too bad. I have only two people at home, so I cannot manage something too fussy. Water from the well is useful, but pumping costs money, so I only water when the crop really needs it.

For wheat, I will do what most people around here do: sow in October on the better fields, use ordinary improved seed from the local dealer, put base fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdressing when the seedlings turn strong after winter. I do not dare cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat gets weak, yield drops fast. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same land. That turnaround is always tight, so I will keep tillage simple and fast. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more watching and more picking by hand. I will not put too much money into cotton, but I will still feed it enough and spray if I see insects. That is safer for my age and for my pocket.
